enquiry: Our existing NIR pilot follows API concentration in one powder formulation at the tablet press feed frame. We are introducing a different API and excipient blend and would like to reuse the calibration. A colleague suggests adding Raman so that the old calibration will remain valid. What should our first technical assessment and experiment be?

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today at the feed frame, and what decision should real-time API concentration data drive for the new blend?
clarification_questions.why: Defines whether the goal is release control, feed adjustment or process understanding, which sets the required accuracy and response.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Goal unclear; provisional assumption is process monitoring for the new blend only, with no control action.

clarification_questions.question: What is the target API concentration range in the new blend, stated in ppm or %?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the method must resolve major or trace components and whether the old calibration range even overlaps.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening establishes whether it is ppm or % level.

clarification_questions.question: What are the physical form, particle size and optical properties of the new blend compared with the existing formulation?
clarification_questions.why: Powder scattering and particle size change NIR and Raman signals and can invalidate a reused calibration.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Assumed to differ from the existing formulation until lab screening shows otherwise.

clarification_questions.question: How does the blend vary at the feed frame (flow, density, moisture, segregation, temperature) and is the fluorescence of the API or excipients known?
clarification_questions.why: Process variation and fluorescence background decide whether Raman can be used at all and how robust a calibration will be.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Variation unknown; treated as a risk until measured in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: What is the probe geometry, distance and optical access at the feed frame, and are any fibers already installed?
clarification_questions.why: Determines the probe type and whether Raman and NIR can measure the same spot.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Access and fiber layout unknown; no probe choice is made until the installation is known.

clarification_questions.question: What reference lab method is used for API concentration, and what is its accuracy for the existing formulation?
clarification_questions.why: Without a reference method and its accuracy, neither calibration transfer nor the value of adding Raman can be judged.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference accuracy available; the lab must establish it on representative samples.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required for the new monitoring task?
clarification_questions.why: Decides whether a single NIR calibration update is enough or a combined method is justified.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the simplest single-method option is assessed first.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: S01 p.10 says overlapping NIR bands suggest the use of chemometrics. It does not say quantification relies on a model built for the measured matrix. Fix: Restate as: overlapping broad NIR bands suggest using chemometrics for quantitative and qualitative analysis (S01 p.10).

not_supported: S01 p.15 describes low-level data fusion of NIR and Raman with PLS models applied to the fused data. It says nothing about whether an existing model is kept or replaced. Fix: Limit the claim to the fused-data PLS approach described on S01 p.15 and drop the statement about not keeping an old model.

overstated: S01 p.12 says Raman spectra can be used to construct calibration or classification chemometric models. It does not say Raman always needs its own calibration. Fix: Say Raman spectra can be used to build their own calibration or classification models (S01 p.12).

not_supported: S01 p.15 names the NIR reflection probe used in the example. Nothing on the cited page states that existing NIR hardware may be retained while a new calibration is built. Fix: Keep only the statement that the example uses an NIR spectrometer with NIR reflection probe (S01 p.15) and remove the retention and recalibration claim.

overstated: S01 p.10 only suggests chemometrics for overlapping bands. It does not state that a model must be built and validated on the new blend. Fix: Rephrase as: overlapping NIR bands suggest chemometric analysis (S01 p.10), so a model should be checked on the new blend.

not_supported: S02 p.6 shows silica fiber ranges (190-2400 nm) and IR fiber ranges, but it does not mention Raman. The claim that silica fibers suit Raman is an inference not stated on the page. Fix: Restrict the fiber statement to the ranges shown on S02 p.6 (silica for UV-VIS and NIR, IR fibers for mid-IR) and state Raman separately, or cite a source page that covers Raman fiber use.

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR probes and general probe use. It does not say that a new API or excipients invalidate an existing calibration. Fix: Rephrase as a risk to verify: a changed formulation may affect the existing calibration and should be checked before reuse, without citing S01 p.10 for that claim.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]
combination_is_hypothesis: Combining methods can add complementary information, but the gain is a hypothesis to test against the best single method. [S01 p.7-8]
raman_fluorescence_background: Raman can be swamped by fluorescence background from many organic compounds; check signal quality first. [S01 p.11]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [guidance]
